The court while directing issue of notice to the Respondents herein to show cause as to why this application should not be complied with, made the following order.(The receipt of this order will be deemed to be the receipt of notice in the case).
ORDER "Heard Sri A.K.Kishore Reddy, learned counsel for the petitioner and Mrs.K.Priyanka Lakshmi,
learned Assistant Public Prosecutor on behalf of the State.
Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the petitioner herein is the accused No.4, who is the elder brother of accused No.1.
The defacto complainant herein is the wife of the accused No.1.
It is a case under Section 49^-A and Sections 3 & 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act which is alleged against the accused No.1, who is the husband and his family members, who are parents and brother.

Learned counsel for the petitioner would further submit that there are no allegations made against the petitioner to either attract the offence under Section 498-A or under the provisions of Dowry Prohibition Act.
Learned counsel for the petitioner would further submit that because of the pendency of the present case against the petitioner herein, his employn^t is at stake.
This Court in the light of the urgency expressed by the learned Public counsel for the petitioner directed the learned Assistant Prosecutor to get instructions from the respondent No.2.
Today, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor would submit that she could not get the Instructions for the respondent No.2 through Police in this matter.
She would further submit that the Court may pass appropriate Orders."^

Considering the submissions and a fair look at the complaint which was submitted to the police by the defacto complainant, as rightly put by the learned counsel for the petitioner, nothing has been alleged against the petitioner.
It further shows that except omnibus allegations that the family members of the husband demanded the defacto complainant Rs.50,000/-, as additional dowry.
